## Motivation

NVFP4 KV cache with FlashInfer speculative prefill needs a dequantized workspace during target verification and draft extend. The prompt-prefill path relies on CPU request/length metadata and a contiguous dequant page table, which do not describe these fixed-width speculative forwards and cannot follow CUDA Graph replay metadata.

This supersedes #36045, which was auto-closed by the idle-PR bot. It refreshes the fix against `888de24cc8a5c919ec952be938c319a36442edbb` and responds to the [SM120 Qwen NVFP4 + MTP report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36045#issuecomment-6078220276).

## Modifications

- Add a capture-stable Triton kernel that reads GPU request indices and lengths, dequantizes cached NVFP4 K/V into their physical FP8 workspace slots, and copies current speculative K/V. Replay can change requests and prefix lengths; padded requests leave reserved slot 0 untouched.
- Route target verification and NVFP4 draft extend through this workspace. Use the current `KVWriteLoc`/`KVLocPlan` APIs and preserve ordinary non-quantized draft-prefill behavior.
- Account for the independent draft pool's full dequant workspace, including implicit MTP. Respect draft KV dtype overrides and the allocator's actual buffer recipe without changing the existing speculative-layer resolver semantics.
- Add CUDA replay tests for 1/2/4 local KV heads, six CPU routing/API-contract tests, and five pool-sizing tests with 15 subcases. Register the GPU test in the Blackwell kernel suite with an executable pytest entry point.

## Accuracy Tests

Executed on an isolated checkout/environment on 2 x RTX 5090 (SM120), using TP2 for the model tests. Runtime: Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, Transformers 5.19.0.

- New CUDA kernel regression: **6 passed**. Bit-exact FP8 workspace comparison against the BF16-intermediate reference, changed request rows/lengths after capture, noncontiguous current K/V, and graph padding.
- CPU pool/speculative-resolver/FP4 regressions: **95 passed, 26 subtests passed** (15 subtests are new).
- New FlashInfer routing/API-contract tests with all GPUs hidden: **6 passed**.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed for all changed files.
- Local `qwen38-27b-nvfp4-modelopt` checkpoint (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, 64 layers) with integrated one-layer MTP, implicit draft path, independent target/draft pools: **all 6 short request groups passed in both graph and eager modes, with exact output-token parity**. This includes repeated BS1/BS2 64-token generation and three simple answer probes. Logs confirm actual CUDA Graph replay at both batch sizes; eager logs show no graph replay.

- Long-context run with context length 131,200 and KV capacity 131,584: **32,768-token and 131,072-token inputs each generated 16 tokens successfully in both modes, with exact graph/eager output-token parity**. All eight request groups in this configuration passed. The long prompts use filler plus a simple instructed response; this is a context smoke test, not a retrieval benchmark. Single-call HTTP times were 4.20/4.98 s (graph/eager) at 32K and 25.10/26.26 s at 128K.

Key model-test flags (no explicit draft model path):

```bash
--tp-size 2 --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-attention-mode prefill \
--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --prefill-kv-cache-dequant-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
--prefill-attention-backend flashinfer --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha \
--fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass --page-size 64 \
--max-running-requests 2 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --disable-radix-cache \
--cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 2
```

The eager comparison replaces the CUDA Graph options with `--disable-cuda-graph`. Both use greedy sampling and the Python TreeCore backend. These are correctness/smoke checks, not a full model accuracy evaluation. RTX PRO 6000 and SM100 model serving were not tested here.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Workspace-kernel-only CUDA Graph replay on one RTX 5090: 2 local KV heads x 256 dimensions (one TP2 rank), 4 current tokens/request, 10 warmup replays followed by 100 timed replays. CUDA-event mean latency:

| Batch | Cached prefix/request | Target verify (ms) | Draft extend (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 32,768 | 0.0756 | 0.0756 |
| 1 | 131,072 | 0.5919 | 0.5919 |
| 2 | 32,768 | 0.2917 | 0.2915 |
| 2 | 131,072 | 1.1756 | 1.1747 |

All eight benchmark configurations passed sampled prefix/current-row oracle checks. These timings cover workspace preparation only; they exclude attention, model forward, TP collectives, and HTTP handling, and do not establish an end-to-end throughput improvement over main.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add and register regression tests.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [x] No user-facing API or CLI change requiring documentation.
- [x] Provide correctness, model smoke/parity, and kernel timing results with scope stated above.

@LingZ315 thanks for the quick refresh! As promised, results from our setup. Short version: **it works on SM120 RTX PRO 6000 in real production traffic** (served our live traffic for ~1 h, 0 errors, 0 tracebacks), quality unchanged, big decode win at long context.

**Setup:** 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (SM120, 96 GB), TP1, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (modelopt mixed) with integrated MTP (`EAGLE` 3/1/4), this PR at `9f285aa`, torch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, sglang-kernel 0.4.9. Flags: `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --prefill-kv-cache-dequant-dtype fp8_e4m3 --attention-backend flashinfer` (decode auto-switched to `trtllm_mha`, page_size forced to 64) `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --prefill-decode-interval 1 --max-mamba-cache-size 250 --max-running-requests 50 --mem-fraction-static 0.90`, no HiCache (per #36121).
Baseline = our production: v0.5.21, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` + HiCache ratio 3, same model/MTP/flags.

**Correctness** (our agent harness, temperature 0.6): tool calls 12/12 (medium) + 12/12 (xhigh), vision 4/4 (skewed invoice OCR, UI screenshot, chart), needle-in-~32k-tokens 4/4. CUDA graphs on, MTP accept length 2.97 vs 3.02 baseline.

**KV capacity:** 990,208 tokens vs 715,591 with FP8 (+38%) at the same mem fraction; 1,075,760 with `--page-size 16 --mem-fraction-static 0.92`.

**Long-context decode** (~84k-token unique prompt, 400 output tokens, measured while serving live traffic):
| | v0.5.21 FP8 KV + HiCache | this PR, NVFP4 KV |
|---|---|---|
| 1 request: TTFT / decode | 14.4 s / 64.2 tok/s | 13.6 s / **102.4 tok/s (+60%)** |
| 4 concurrent: TTFT / decode | 35.2 s / 25.8 tok/s | 34.8 s / 22.5 tok/s |

**Live traffic, warm cache** (our agent workload, 25–60k-token contexts):
- Chunked-prefill throughput +17% (6,349 vs 5,449 tok/s per 16k chunk), probably main vs 0.5.21 rather than this PR.
- Per-request decode at mid-length contexts (25–30k) ~10% lower than baseline (121 vs 134 tok/s at 1–2 running, 97 vs 111 at 3–5); end-to-end median at our gateway +7% (110 vs 103 tok/s).
- Prefix-cache hit rate 80% vs 86%: we lose HiCache (#36121) and page_size 64 (forced by `trtllm_mha`) coarsens prefix reuse.

**Notes:**
1. First requests after start trigger JIT compilation (ptxas/Triton) that blocks the scheduler: `/health` failed for ~2 min and our gateway marked the backend down. A warm-up at startup (or compiling during graph capture) would avoid that.
2. The decode win grows with context length, the mid-context regression is small; together with #36121 (HiCache scale buffers) this would be a clear upgrade for us.

Thanks again, happy to re-test follow-ups.

Follow-up with HiCache back on: #43356 + #43240 (HiCache FP4 host-pool fix, validated in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43240#issuecomment-6084684345), same SM120 setup, `--hicache-ratio 3`, page_size 64, mem 0.90. Served production for ~40 min, 0 errors, MTP accept 2.88, quality checks unchanged — so the PR itself is solid on SM120.

Throughput, live agent traffic with warm cache (most contexts 25–35k tokens), vs our v0.5.21 FP8 KV + FlashInfer + HiCache baseline at similar load:
| | baseline | #43356 + #43240 |
|---|---|---|
| per-request decode, 1–2 running | ~134 tok/s | 106 tok/s |
| per-request decode, 3–5 running | ~111 tok/s | 82 tok/s |
| prefix-cache hit | 86% | 77% |
| end-to-end median at our gateway | 103–118 tok/s | 86 tok/s |

So on SM120 the NVFP4 path wins clearly only at long context (+60% decode at ~84k, earlier comment) and loses ~20–25% at mid-length contexts. Our guess is the mandatory `trtllm_mha` (XQA) decode for NVFP4 on SM120 plus page_size 64 (lower prefix reuse), not your workspace kernel. We're back on FP8 KV for now and will re-test when the SM120 NVFP4 decode path or page-size constraint changes. Thanks again!

@AppNetDeveloper your data is exactly why we shipped #43471 last night — same SM120 platform, same Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + MTP stack. It may change the tradeoff you backed away from.

To be precise about what it does *not* touch: your mid-length decode regression (~134→106 tok/s at 1–2 running) is on the trtllm_mha/XQA **decode** path + page-64 reuse, and #43471 doesn't move decode kernels — your conclusion holds there. What #43471 removes is the FP8 dequant **workspace** from the prefill path entirely: NVFP4 prefill now goes through FlashInfer's native packed-FP4 paged prefill (`run(..., kv_cache_sf=...)`, kernel-side tile dequant), so the per-chunk gather→bf16→fp8 re-dequant of the whole cached prefix is gone — along with its two structural taxes:

- **Transient memory**: on our 2× RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (TP2) rig, a ~45K-token cold prefix OOM-killed the scheduler *in production* via `dequantize_prev_kv` temporaries under the workspace route. With #43471, back-to-back cold 45K/100K/150K prefill rounds run with GPU memory **flat to the MiB** across all rounds (no per-layer spikes at all).
- **Fixed + per-token pool cost**: `dq_k/dq_v` were allocated per pool-row (~146 MiB/rank) *and* charged 1024 B/token into `compute_cell_size`. Both vanish → cell size 10816→**9792 B/token**, i.e. **+10.5% same-budget pool capacity**, and boot headroom rose 0.88→2.6 GB/rank at our 180K config, which let us raise both pool and mamba-slot budget.

Reference numbers (same rig, native-FP4 prefill, greedy, cold disjoint prefixes — full A/B vs the workspace route running as I type; these are the absolute values):

| metric | 2×5060 Ti 16GB TP2 (chunk 2048) |
|---|---|
| 45K cold prefill TTFT | 12.4 s |
| 100K cold | 35.5 s |
| 150K cold | in-flight (180K pool, usage ~0.83) |
| decode (NEXTN 2/1/3 MTP) | 70–90 tok/s single-stream, accept 2.1–3.0, HiCache kernel+`#43240` battery green |

Notes for a trial on your rig:
- #43471 is `main`-based and env-gated: `SGLANG_NVFP4_NATIVE_PREFILL=0` restores the old workspace route for a clean A/B with no re-deploy.
- It expects FlashInfer's NVFP4 `kv_cache_sf` prefill support (present in 0.6.18; worth a quick check on your 0.7.0.post1 before wiring).
- Expect a minor rebase conflict against #43356 — both touch the same forward path, but #43356's spec-extend workspace kernels and this route are orthogonal (spec verify/draft-extend still rides trtllm native decode). Happy to help resolve a combined tree.
- Your chunked-prefill 16384 already shrinks the workspace route's quadratic re-dequant tax (fewer chunks), so the prefill *time* delta may be modest for you; the OOM-class removal and the +10.5% capacity / headroom are the parts that don't depend on chunk size.

If the decode side is what keeps you on FP8 KV, one data point worth having on your radar: on SM120 the decode loss looks like an XQA/page-size property of the NVFP4 route, not of the KV format's arithmetic — if FP8-KV decode at page 64 ≈ page 16 on your harness, the mid-length story may be fixable independently of this.

@chengye75-star @LingZ315 thanks for the pointer to #43471. We tried it on the same SM120 setup. Short version: native NVFP4 prefill + MTP verify is **correct but crashes under CUDA graphs at bs=16**, and on SM120 there is currently no graph-safe native verify path.

**Tree:** #43356 @ `9f285aa` + #43240 (HiCache FP4 host pool) + #43471 @ `4eae8ca` cherry-picked. There was one conflict in `FlashInferAttnBackend.forward_extend`. We put the `prefill_uses_native_fp4` branch first and kept #43356's speculative/regular dequant-workspace branches as the `elif`. That means that, with native prefill on, target verify and draft extend also read the packed pool through `run(..., kv_cache_sf=...)`.
**Setup:** 1× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), TP1, Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (ThinkingCap A4 checkpoint, hybrid GDN), EAGLE 3/1/4, `speculative_attention_mode=prefill` (default on SM120), `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --prefill-kv-cache-dequant-dtype fp8_e4m3`, HiCache ratio 3, page 64, mem 0.90, `SGLANG_NVFP4_NATIVE_PREFILL=1`.

**What works**
- KV pool **1,187,136 tokens** vs 709,511 with FP8 KV at the same mem fraction (+67%). With #43356 alone we had ~990k, so the freed workspace shows up as expected.
- Without decode CUDA graphs (`--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled`): no errors, and our harness all passes (reasoning 16/16, tool calls 24/24, vision 4/4, needle 4/4). MTP accept len matches FP8 KV: 3.15 vs 3.16 at 1–4 running, 2.49 vs 2.52 at 10–19. So the numerics of the native verify path look right.

**What breaks (decode CUDA graphs on)**
Fine at low concurrency (accept 3.15 at 1–4 running). On a 16-concurrent decode burst, the scheduler died after ~6 s:
```
eagle_worker_v2.verify -> run_eagle_verify -> eagle_prepare_for_verify
-> decode_cuda_graph_runner.load_batch -> hybrid_attn_backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph
-> flashinfer_backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph -> indices_updater_prefill.update
-> wrapper_paged.begin_forward/plan -> _compute_page_mask_indptr: mask_indptr[0] = 0
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```
The error is async, so the faulting kernel is probably the previous graph replay of target verify through the native `kv_cache_sf` route, not `plan()` itself. Our guess: something the native route reads at replay isn't graph-stable for the bs=16 graph. Candidates are the wrapper attributes injected by `_set_paged_forward_attrs` at capture time, or plan buffers sized for the dequant-workspace route. Same tree, same traffic, graphs off → clean.

**`--speculative-attention-mode decode` (verify on trtllm_mha) does not start on SM120**
```
Capture cuda graph failed: shape '[1187200, 4, 256]' is invalid for input of size 607846400
```
The trtllm verify path views the packed FP4 pool (`head_dim // 2`) as unpacked. As `kv_cache_hook` says, native trtllm verify is SM100-only today.

**Why this matters on SM120:** the only graph-safe verify path today is #43356's speculative dequant workspace. It re-dequantizes every running request's whole cached prefix into FP8 on every verify step. We suspect that is behind the −20–25% mid-context (25–35k) decode we reported earlier. A graph-safe native verify (#43471's route) would likely remove it and keep the +67% capacity.

FP8 KV baseline on the same box for reference (unique prefixes, 400 output tokens, per-request decode): ~27k: 124.5 tok/s c1 / 57.8 c4 / 37.2 c8 · ~50k: 105.0 c1 / 24.1 c8 · ~141k: 83.5 c1 / 22.3 c4. Happy to run a fix on this rig and report the same table for NVFP4.

[@AppNetDeveloper](https://github.com/AppNetDeveloper) your bs=16 crash report was exactly the evidence we needed — thank you. Confirmed: the gap is in our PR, not in your merge. #43471's native branch as written covers `forward_extend` unconditionally, so with your (correct) conflict resolution your speculative forwards went native — and graph-stability of the native `kv_cache_sf` path had only ever been exercised at bs≤2 (our rig captures [1,2] only). Your async-error reading and both suspects are spot on.

**Fix pushed to the PR branch** (`feat/nvfp4-native-prefill`, commit 00f2216):
- The native FP4 route is now guarded to **plain prompt-prefill only**. Target verify / draft extend (v2) are downgraded to the dequant-workspace branch — i.e. on your tree, #43356's graph-safe speculative workspace path takes over exactly as before the cherry-pick.
- Plan dtype follows the downgrade: when a speculative wrapper is planned with `spec_info` present while native prefill is on, `kv_data_type` is passed as `float8_e4m3fn` instead of the packed `uint8` — a static dtype here was very plausibly the IMA you saw (fp8 workspace tensors planned as packed bytes, or vice versa, at capture vs replay).
- Pool accounting is untouched, so the +67% capacity (no per-row workspace, 9792 B/token) stays regardless of the guard.
- An operator opt-in `SGLANG_NVFP4_NATIVE_SPEC=1` exists for rigs whose decode-graph capture list is provably small (ours: [1,2], where native verify runs at accept 2.9–3.0 with the full HiCache battery green). Default is off; on the bare PR base the fallback branch needs #43356's speculative workspace — we say that plainly in the docstring rather than pretend bare-main spec is supported.

**What we ask you to re-test on the PRO 6000** (we can't reach bs=16 on 16 GB×2 — your rig is the only bs=16 evidence that matters):
1. #43356 @ `9f285aa` + #43240 + refreshed #43471 (take the branch head, re-resolve the one `forward_extend` conflict — the guard is inside the native branch condition, your native-first ordering should now drop spec onto your #43356 elif automatically), decode CUDA graphs **enabled**, burst at the same 16-concurrency that killed the scheduler in ~6 s.
2. Same quality set (reasoning/tool/vision/needle) and accept at 1–4 and 10–19 running, to confirm the downgrade is numerically free (workspace route was your passing baseline in the first report).
3. If it comes back clean, the same decode table you posted for FP8 KV (27k/50k/141k, c1/c4/c8) — that turns the guard into a full tradeoff picture for the maintainers: native cold-prefill + OOM fix + pool gain, spec verify on the graph-safe workspace until a graph-stable native verify lands.

On that last point we agree with your framing: a genuinely graph-safe native verify (stable plan buffers across replays at captured shapes) is the real prize, and your `plan()`-vs-replay analysis in the crash note is the right starting map. We're working it; when we have a candidate we would very much like your harness on it.

Reference, same-PR guard build on our SM120 TP2 rig just now: decode 90.4 (counting) / 76.9 (short) / 70.5 (creative), cold prefill 45K/100K at 12.2/34.9 s, memory flat — bit-for-bit the same as ungarded native, as expected for a guard that only moves speculative forwards.

+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.nvfp4_kv_cache import (
+    dequantize_nvfp4_kv_for_speculative_extend,
+)
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.kvfp4_tensor import E2M1_VALUES
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_sm100_supported, is_sm120_supported

+)

+def _dequantize_reference(fp4_data, block_scales, global_scale):
+    unpacked = torch.empty(
+        *fp4_data.shape[:-1],
+        fp4_data.shape[-1] * 2,
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        device=fp4_data.device,
+    )
+    unpacked[..., 0::2] = fp4_data & 0xF
+    unpacked[..., 1::2] = (fp4_data >> 4) & 0xF
+    values = torch.tensor(E2M1_VALUES, dtype=torch.float32, device=fp4_data.device)
+    return (
+        (
+            values[unpacked.long()]
+            * block_scales.float().repeat_interleave(16, dim=-1)
+            * global_scale
+        )
+        .to(torch.bfloat16)
+        .to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    )
+
+

+    not (is_sm100_supported() or is_sm120_supported()),
+    reason="NVFP4 KV cache requires SM100 or SM120",
+)

+)

+def test_speculative_workspace_graph_replay_uses_runtime_lengths(
+    prefix_len_delta, heads, head_dim
+):
+    torch.manual_seed(7)
+    device = "cuda"
+    size = 64
+    real_batch_size, graph_batch_size = 2, 3
+    current_tokens_per_req, max_context = 4, 16
+
+    k_fp4 = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (size, heads, head_dim // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+    )
+    v_fp4 = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (size, heads, head_dim // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+    )
+    k_block_scales = (torch.rand(size, heads, head_dim // 16, device=device) * 0.2).to(
+        torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    )
+    v_block_scales = (torch.rand(size, heads, head_dim // 16, device=device) * 0.2).to(
+        torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    )
+    k_global_scale = torch.tensor([0.02], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    v_global_scale = torch.tensor([0.03], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+
+    req_to_token = torch.zeros(
+        real_batch_size + 1, max_context, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+    )
+    req_to_token[0] = torch.arange(2, 18, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    req_to_token[1] = torch.arange(22, 38, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    req_to_token[2] = torch.arange(42, 58, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    # The third row models CUDA Graph padding: graph buffers use request row 0
+    # and reserved KV slot 0 for padded requests.
+    req_pool_indices = torch.tensor([0, 1, 0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    sequence_lens = torch.tensor(
+        [1 + prefix_len_delta, 2 + prefix_len_delta, 1],
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device=device,
+    )
+
+    # QKV splits can have a larger per-token stride. Exercise that layout so
+    # target verify does not add a contiguous() allocation inside the graph.
+    num_current_rows = graph_batch_size * current_tokens_per_req
+    k_current_storage = torch.randn(
+        num_current_rows,
+        heads * head_dim + 13,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    v_current_storage = torch.randn(
+        num_current_rows,
+        heads * head_dim + 17,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    k_current = k_current_storage[:, : heads * head_dim].view(
+        num_current_rows, heads, head_dim
+    )
+    v_current = v_current_storage[:, : heads * head_dim].view(
+        num_current_rows, heads, head_dim
+    )

+    assert not v_current.is_contiguous()

+        dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+        device=device,

+    def make_current_locs(real_prefix_lens, request_rows):
+        locs = torch.zeros(
+            graph_batch_size,
+            current_tokens_per_req,
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device=device,

+        for req_offset, prefix_len in enumerate(real_prefix_lens):
+            locs[req_offset].copy_(

+                    request_rows[req_offset],

+    current_locs = make_current_locs([1, 2], [0, 1])
+
+    def run_kernel():
+        dequantize_nvfp4_kv_for_speculative_extend(
+            k_fp4,
+            v_fp4,
+            k_block_scales,
+            v_block_scales,
+            k_global_scale,
+            v_global_scale,
+            k_current,
+            v_current,
+            dq_k,
+            dq_v,
+            req_to_token,
+            req_pool_indices,
+            sequence_lens,
+            current_locs,
+            current_tokens_per_req,
+            prefix_len_delta,
+        )
+
+    # Compile before capture, then capture with short prefixes.
+    run_kernel()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        run_kernel()
+
+    # Replay the same graph with different device-resident requests and lengths.
+    # Capture-time host metadata would leave the new request's prefix as NaN.
+    dq_k.fill_(float("nan"))
+    dq_v.fill_(float("nan"))
+    replay_prefix_lens = [6, 7]
+    replay_request_rows = [1, 2]
+    req_pool_indices.copy_(torch.tensor([1, 2, 0], device=device))
+    sequence_lens.copy_(
+        torch.tensor(
+            [
+                *(length + prefix_len_delta for length in replay_prefix_lens),
+                1,
+            ],
+            device=device,
+        )
+    )
+    current_locs.copy_(make_current_locs(replay_prefix_lens, replay_request_rows))
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    k_prefix_reference = _dequantize_reference(k_fp4, k_block_scales, k_global_scale)
+    v_prefix_reference = _dequantize_reference(v_fp4, v_block_scales, v_global_scale)
+    for req_offset, prefix_len in enumerate(replay_prefix_lens):
+        request_row = replay_request_rows[req_offset]
+        prefix_slots = req_to_token[request_row, :prefix_len].long()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            dq_k[prefix_slots].float(),
+            k_prefix_reference[prefix_slots].float(),
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            dq_v[prefix_slots].float(),
+            v_prefix_reference[prefix_slots].float(),
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+
+        current_slots = req_to_token[
+            request_row,
+            prefix_len : prefix_len + current_tokens_per_req,
+        ].long()
+        current_rows = slice(
+            req_offset * current_tokens_per_req,
+            (req_offset + 1) * current_tokens_per_req,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            dq_k[current_slots].float(),
+            k_current[current_rows].to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float(),
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            dq_v[current_slots].float(),
+            v_current[current_rows].to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float(),
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+
+    # Padded requests must not write slot 0 or reuse the capture-time request 0.
+    for workspace in (dq_k, dq_v):
+        assert torch.isnan(workspace[0].float()).all()
+        assert torch.isnan(workspace[req_to_token[0].long()].float()).all()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

+        # and a shared FP8 workspace. SM120 reuses linear scales for native reads.
+        for prefill, native_layout, expected in [
+            ("flashinfer", True, 12_544),
+            ("flashinfer", False, 11_392),
+            ("trtllm_mha", True, 10_368),
+            ("trtllm_mha", False, 10_368),
+        ]:
+            with self.subTest(prefill=prefill, native_layout=native_layout):
+                cfg, config = self._fp4_eagle_config(
+                    prefill_backend=prefill, native_scale_layout=native_layout
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(cfg._cell_size, expected)
+                self.assertLessEqual(config.max_total_num_tokens * expected, 10_000_000)
+
+    def test_fp4_eagle_reserves_implicit_mtp_private_pool(self):
+        # The resolver keeps eagle_draft_num_layers=None for path-less MTP.
+        # Its draft-mode KV layer count must still reserve a separate FP4 pool.
+        for prefill, native_layout, expected in [
+            ("flashinfer", True, 11_584),
+            ("flashinfer", False, 10_528),
+            ("trtllm_mha", True, 9_504),
+            ("trtllm_mha", False, 9_504),
+        ]:
+            with self.subTest(prefill=prefill, native_layout=native_layout):
+                cfg, config = self._fp4_eagle_config(
+                    prefill_backend=prefill,
+                    native_scale_layout=native_layout,
+                    draft_layers=1,
+                    implicit_mtp=True,
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(cfg._cell_size, expected)
+                self.assertLessEqual(config.max_total_num_tokens * expected, 10_000_000)
+
+    def test_fp4_eagle_draft_backend_keeps_allocator_selected_buffers(self):
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_kv_cache_quant_method import (
+            NVFP4KVCacheMethod,
+        )
+        from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv_cache_configurator import KVCacheConfigurator
+
+        for target_prefill, draft_backend, target_cost, expected in [
+            ("flashinfer", "trtllm_mha", 10_752, 12_544),
+            ("trtllm_mha", "flashinfer", 9_216, 10_368),
+        ]:
+            with self.subTest(target=target_prefill, draft=draft_backend):
+                cfg, _ = self._fp4_eagle_config(
+                    prefill_backend=target_prefill, draft_backend=draft_backend
+                )
+                # Exercise the actual allocation recipe: the configurator reads
+                # the shared server_args, regardless of the draft execution backend.
+                allocator = object.__new__(KVCacheConfigurator)
+                allocator.kv_cache_dtype = torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2
+                allocator.kv_cache_dtype_str = "nvfp4"
+                allocator.device = "cpu"
+                allocator.page_size = 1
+                allocator.server_args = get_server_args()
+                allocator.model = None
+                with (
+                    patch(
+                        "sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_kv_cache_quant_method."
+                        "get_platform",
+                        return_value=SimpleNamespace(is_sm100=True),
+                    ),
+                    patch.object(NVFP4KVCacheMethod, "load_scales_from_model"),
+                ):
+                    method = allocator._build_fp4_quant_method(num_layers=4)
+                    allocated_draft_cost = method.compute_cell_size(4, 64, 4, 1)
+                self.assertEqual(cfg._cell_size, expected)
+                self.assertEqual(cfg._cell_size, target_cost + allocated_draft_cost)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    method.needs_dequant_workspace(), target_prefill == "flashinfer"
+                )
+
+    def test_fp4_eagle_respects_draft_dtype_override(self):
+        for draft_dtype, expected in [
+            ("bf16", 14_848),
+            ("fp8_e4m3", 12_800),
+            # The draft's loaded quant config may reduce this conservative cost.
+            ("auto", 14_848),
+        ]:
+            with self.subTest(draft_dtype=draft_dtype):
+                cfg, _ = self._fp4_eagle_config(
+                    prefill_backend="flashinfer", draft_dtype=draft_dtype
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(cfg._cell_size, expected)
+                from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv_cache_dtype import configure_kv_cache_dtype
+
+                # This is the loaded draft's dtype resolution. For auto, a model
+                # quant config can choose FP8; reserving BF16 must still fit it.
+                loaded_draft = SimpleNamespace(
+                    quant_config=SimpleNamespace(kv_cache_quant_algo="FP8")
+                )
+                _, allocated_dtype = configure_kv_cache_dtype(
+                    server_args_kv_cache_dtype="nvfp4",
+                    speculative_draft_kv_cache_dtype=draft_dtype,
+                    model=loaded_draft,
+                    model_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                    is_draft_worker=True,
+                    is_dflash=False,
+                    speculative_draft_attention_backend=None,
+                )
+                actual_draft_cost = 4 * (64 + 64) * 4 * allocated_dtype.itemsize
+                self.assertGreaterEqual(cfg._cell_size, 10_752 + actual_draft_cost)
+                if draft_dtype != "auto":
+                    self.assertEqual(cfg._cell_size, 10_752 + actual_draft_cost)
+
+    def test_fp4_eagle_fused_entry_is_not_charged_a_private_pool(self):
+        for implicit_mtp in [False, True]:
+            with self.subTest(implicit_mtp=implicit_mtp):
+                cfg, config = self._fp4_eagle_config(
+                    prefill_backend="flashinfer",
+                    implicit_mtp=implicit_mtp,
+                    fused_entry=12_000,
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(cfg._cell_size, 12_000)
+                self.assertLessEqual(config.max_total_num_tokens * 12_000, 10_000_000)
+
     @patch(
         "sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv_cache_configurator.calculate_mla_kv_cache_dim",

@LingZ315 thanks for the quick refresh! As promised, results from our setup. Short version: **it works on SM120 RTX PRO 6000 in real production traffic** (served our live traffic for ~1 h, 0 errors, 0 tracebacks), quality unchanged, big decode win at long context.

**Setup:** 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (SM120, 96 GB), TP1, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (modelopt mixed) with integrated MTP (`EAGLE` 3/1/4), this PR at `9f285aa`, torch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, sglang-kernel 0.4.9. Flags: `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --prefill-kv-cache-dequant-dtype fp8_e4m3 --attention-backend flashinfer` (decode auto-switched to `trtllm_mha`, page_size forced to 64) `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --prefill-decode-interval 1 --max-mamba-cache-size 250 --max-running-requests 50 --mem-fraction-static 0.90`, no HiCache (per #36121).
Baseline = our production: v0.5.21, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` + HiCache ratio 3, same model/MTP/flags.

**Correctness** (our agent harness, temperature 0.6): tool calls 12/12 (medium) + 12/12 (xhigh), vision 4/4 (skewed invoice OCR, UI screenshot, chart), needle-in-~32k-tokens 4/4. CUDA graphs on, MTP accept length 2.97 vs 3.02 baseline.

**KV capacity:** 990,208 tokens vs 715,591 with FP8 (+38%) at the same mem fraction; 1,075,760 with `--page-size 16 --mem-fraction-static 0.92`.

**Long-context decode** (~84k-token unique prompt, 400 output tokens, measured while serving live traffic):
| | v0.5.21 FP8 KV + HiCache | this PR, NVFP4 KV |
|---|---|---|
| 1 request: TTFT / decode | 14.4 s / 64.2 tok/s | 13.6 s / **102.4 tok/s (+60%)** |
| 4 concurrent: TTFT / decode | 35.2 s / 25.8 tok/s | 34.8 s / 22.5 tok/s |

**Live traffic, warm cache** (our agent workload, 25–60k-token contexts):
- Chunked-prefill throughput +17% (6,349 vs 5,449 tok/s per 16k chunk), probably main vs 0.5.21 rather than this PR.
- Per-request decode at mid-length contexts (25–30k) ~10% lower than baseline (121 vs 134 tok/s at 1–2 running, 97 vs 111 at 3–5); end-to-end median at our gateway +7% (110 vs 103 tok/s).
- Prefix-cache hit rate 80% vs 86%: we lose HiCache (#36121) and page_size 64 (forced by `trtllm_mha`) coarsens prefix reuse.

**Notes:**
1. First requests after start trigger JIT compilation (ptxas/Triton) that blocks the scheduler: `/health` failed for ~2 min and our gateway marked the backend down. A warm-up at startup (or compiling during graph capture) would avoid that.
2. The decode win grows with context length, the mid-context regression is small; together with #36121 (HiCache scale buffers) this would be a clear upgrade for us.

Thanks again, happy to re-test follow-ups.

Follow-up with HiCache back on: #43356 + #43240 (HiCache FP4 host-pool fix, validated in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43240#issuecomment-6084684345), same SM120 setup, `--hicache-ratio 3`, page_size 64, mem 0.90. Served production for ~40 min, 0 errors, MTP accept 2.88, quality checks unchanged — so the PR itself is solid on SM120.

Throughput, live agent traffic with warm cache (most contexts 25–35k tokens), vs our v0.5.21 FP8 KV + FlashInfer + HiCache baseline at similar load:
| | baseline | #43356 + #43240 |
|---|---|---|
| per-request decode, 1–2 running | ~134 tok/s | 106 tok/s |
| per-request decode, 3–5 running | ~111 tok/s | 82 tok/s |
| prefix-cache hit | 86% | 77% |

So on SM120 the NVFP4 path wins clearly only at long context (+60% decode at ~84k, earlier comment) and loses ~20–25% at mid-length contexts. Our guess is the mandatory `trtllm_mha` (XQA) decode for NVFP4 on SM120 plus page_size 64 (lower prefix reuse), not your workspace kernel. @AppNetDeveloper your data is exactly why we shipped #43471 last night — same SM120 platform, same Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + MTP stack. It may change the tradeoff you backed away from.

To be precise about what it does *not* touch: your mid-length decode regression (~134→106 tok/s at 1–2 running) is on the trtllm_mha/XQA **decode** path + page-64 reuse, and #43471 doesn't move decode kernels — your conclusion holds there. What #43471 removes is the FP8 dequant **workspace** from the prefill path entirely: NVFP4 prefill now goes through FlashInfer's native packed-FP4 paged prefill (`run(..., kv_cache_sf=...)`, kernel-side tile dequant), so the per-chunk gather→bf16→fp8 re-dequant of the whole cached prefix is gone — along with its two structural taxes:

- **Transient memory**: on our 2× RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (TP2) rig, a ~45K-token cold prefix OOM-killed the scheduler *in production* via `dequantize_prev_kv` temporaries under the workspace route. With #43471, back-to-back cold 45K/100K/150K prefill rounds run with GPU memory **flat to the MiB** across all rounds (no per-layer spikes at all).
- **Fixed + per-token pool cost**: `dq_k/dq_v` were allocated per pool-row (~146 MiB/rank) *and* charged 1024 B/token into `compute_cell_size`. Both vanish → cell size 10816→**9792 B/token**, i.e. **+10.5% same-budget pool capacity**, and boot headroom rose 0.88→2.6 GB/rank at our 180K config, which let us raise both pool and mamba-slot budget.

Reference numbers (same rig, native-FP4 prefill, greedy, cold disjoint prefixes — full A/B vs the workspace route running as I type; these are the absolute values):

| metric | 2×5060 Ti 16GB TP2 (chunk 2048) |
|---|---|
| 45K cold prefill TTFT | 12.4 s |
| 100K cold | 35.5 s |
| 150K cold | in-flight (180K pool, usage ~0.83) |
| decode (NEXTN 2/1/3 MTP) | 70–90 tok/s single-stream, accept 2.1–3.0, HiCache kernel+`#43240` battery green |

Notes for a trial on your rig:
- #43471 is `main`-based and env-gated: `SGLANG_NVFP4_NATIVE_PREFILL=0` restores the old workspace route for a clean A/B with no re-deploy.
- It expects FlashInfer's NVFP4 `kv_cache_sf` prefill support (present in 0.6.18; worth a quick check on your 0.7.0.post1 before wiring).
- Expect a minor rebase conflict against #43356 — both touch the same forward path, but #43356's spec-extend workspace kernels and this route are orthogonal (spec verify/draft-extend still rides trtllm native decode). Happy to help resolve a combined tree.
- Your chunked-prefill 16384 already shrinks the workspace route's quadratic re-dequant tax (fewer chunks), so the prefill *time* delta may be modest for you; the OOM-class removal and the +10.5% capacity / headroom are the parts that don't depend on chunk size.

If the decode side is what keeps you on FP8 KV, one data point worth having on your radar: on SM120 the decode loss looks like an XQA/page-size property of the NVFP4 route, not of the KV format's arithmetic — if FP8-KV decode at page 64 ≈ page 16 on your harness, the mid-length story may be fixable independently of this.

@chengye75-star @LingZ315 thanks for the pointer to #43471. We tried it on the same SM120 setup. Short version: native NVFP4 prefill + MTP verify is **correct but crashes under CUDA graphs at bs=16**, and on SM120 there is currently no graph-safe native verify path.

**Tree:** #43356 @ `9f285aa` + #43240 (HiCache FP4 host pool) + #43471 @ `4eae8ca` cherry-picked. There was one conflict in `FlashInferAttnBackend.forward_extend`. We put the `prefill_uses_native_fp4` branch first and kept #43356's speculative/regular dequant-workspace branches as the `elif`. That means that, with native prefill on, target verify and draft extend also read the packed pool through `run(..., kv_cache_sf=...)`.
**Setup:** 1× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), TP1, Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (ThinkingCap A4 checkpoint, hybrid GDN), EAGLE 3/1/4, `speculative_attention_mode=prefill` (default on SM120), `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --prefill-kv-cache-dequant-dtype fp8_e4m3`, HiCache ratio 3, page 64, mem 0.90, `SGLANG_NVFP4_NATIVE_PREFILL=1`.

**What works**
- KV pool **1,187,136 tokens** vs 709,511 with FP8 KV at the same mem fraction (+67%). With #43356 alone we had ~990k, so the freed workspace shows up as expected.
- Without decode CUDA graphs (`--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled`): no errors, and our harness all passes (reasoning 16/16, tool calls 24/24, vision 4/4, needle 4/4). MTP accept len matches FP8 KV: 3.15 vs 3.16 at 1–4 running, 2.49 vs 2.52 at 10–19. So the numerics of the native verify path look right.

**What breaks (decode CUDA graphs on)**
Fine at low concurrency (accept 3.15 at 1–4 running). On a 16-concurrent decode burst, the scheduler died after ~6 s:
```
eagle_worker_v2.verify -> run_eagle_verify -> eagle_prepare_for_verify
-> decode_cuda_graph_runner.load_batch -> hybrid_attn_backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph
-> flashinfer_backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph -> indices_updater_prefill.update
-> wrapper_paged.begin_forward/plan -> _compute_page_mask_indptr: mask_indptr[0] = 0
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```
The error is async, so the faulting kernel is probably the previous graph replay of target verify through the native `kv_cache_sf` route, not `plan()` itself. Our guess: something the native route reads at replay isn't graph-stable for the bs=16 graph. Candidates are the wrapper attributes injected by `_set_paged_forward_attrs` at capture time, or plan buffers sized for the dequant-workspace route. Same tree, same traffic, graphs off → clean.

**`--speculative-attention-mode decode` (verify on trtllm_mha) does not start on SM120**
```
Capture cuda graph failed: shape '[1187200, 4, 256]' is invalid for input of size 607846400
```
The trtllm verify path views the packed FP4 pool (`head_dim // 2`) as unpacked. As `kv_cache_hook` says, native trtllm verify is SM100-only today.

**Why this matters on SM120:** the only graph-safe verify path today is #43356's speculative dequant workspace. It re-dequantizes every running request's whole cached prefix into FP8 on every verify step. We suspect that is behind the −20–25% mid-context (25–35k) decode we reported earlier. A graph-safe native verify (#43471's route) would likely remove it and keep the +67% capacity.

FP8 KV baseline on the same box for reference (unique prefixes, 400 output tokens, per-request decode): ~27k: 124.5 tok/s c1 / 57.8 c4 / 37.2 c8 · ~50k: 105.0 c1 / 24.1 c8 · ~141k: 83.5 c1 / 22.3 c4. Happy to run a fix on this rig and report the same table for NVFP4.

[@AppNetDeveloper](https://github.com/AppNetDeveloper) your bs=16 crash report was exactly the evidence we needed — thank you. Confirmed: the gap is in our PR, not in your merge. #43471's native branch as written covers `forward_extend` unconditionally, so with your (correct) conflict resolution your speculative forwards went native — and graph-stability of the native `kv_cache_sf` path had only ever been exercised at bs≤2 (our rig captures [1,2] only). Your async-error reading and both suspects are spot on.

**Fix pushed to the PR branch** (`feat/nvfp4-native-prefill`, commit 00f2216):
- The native FP4 route is now guarded to **plain prompt-prefill only**. Target verify / draft extend (v2) are downgraded to the dequant-workspace branch — i.e. on your tree, #43356's graph-safe speculative workspace path takes over exactly as before the cherry-pick.
- Plan dtype follows the downgrade: when a speculative wrapper is planned with `spec_info` present while native prefill is on, `kv_data_type` is passed as `float8_e4m3fn` instead of the packed `uint8` — a static dtype here was very plausibly the IMA you saw (fp8 workspace tensors planned as packed bytes, or vice versa, at capture vs replay).
- Pool accounting is untouched, so the +67% capacity (no per-row workspace, 9792 B/token) stays regardless of the guard.
- An operator opt-in `SGLANG_NVFP4_NATIVE_SPEC=1` exists for rigs whose decode-graph capture list is provably small (ours: [1,2], where native verify runs at accept 2.9–3.0 with the full HiCache battery green). Default is off; on the bare PR base the fallback branch needs #43356's speculative workspace — we say that plainly in the docstring rather than pretend bare-main spec is supported.

**What we ask you to re-test on the PRO 6000** (we can't reach bs=16 on 16 GB×2 — your rig is the only bs=16 evidence that matters):
1. #43356 @ `9f285aa` + #43240 + refreshed #43471 (take the branch head, re-resolve the one `forward_extend` conflict — the guard is inside the native branch condition, your native-first ordering should now drop spec onto your #43356 elif automatically), decode CUDA graphs **enabled**, burst at the same 16-concurrency that killed the scheduler in ~6 s.
2. Same quality set (reasoning/tool/vision/needle) and accept at 1–4 and 10–19 running, to confirm the downgrade is numerically free (workspace route was your passing baseline in the first report).
3. If it comes back clean, the same decode table you posted for FP8 KV (27k/50k/141k, c1/c4/c8) — that turns the guard into a full tradeoff picture for the maintainers: native cold-prefill + OOM fix + pool gain, spec verify on the graph-safe workspace until a graph-stable native verify lands.

On that last point we agree with your framing: a genuinely graph-safe native verify (stable plan buffers across replays at captured shapes) is the real prize, and your `plan()`-vs-replay analysis in the crash note is the right starting map. We're working it; when we have a candidate we would very much like your harness on it.

Reference, same-PR guard build on our SM120 TP2 rig just now: decode 90.4 (counting) / 76.9 (short) / 70.5 (creative), cold prefill 45K/100K at 12.2/34.9 s, memory flat — bit-for-bit the same as ungarded native, as expected for a guard that only moves speculative forwards.
